ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Oxygen is carried in the blood by the respiratory pigment hemoglobin, which can combine loosely with four oxygen molecules to form the molecule oxyhemoglobin. To function properly, hemoglobin must bind to oxygen in the lungs and drop it off at body cells. The more easily the hemoglobin bonds to oxygen in the lungs, the more difficult for the hemoglobin to unload the oxygen at the body cells. Here is a graph showing two different saturation-dissociation curves for one type of hemoglobin at two different pH levels.

Based on your knowledge of biology and the information in this graph, which statement about the hemoglobin curves is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When CO2 levels in the blood are high, as shown in hemoglobin B, hemoglobin releases oxygen more readily.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph shows O2 saturation of hemoglobin on the y-axis versus PO2 on the x-axis. There are two sigmoidal oxygen saturation curves: curve A is the upper/left-shifted dashed curve near pH 7.4, and curve B is the lower/right-shifted solid curve near pH 7.2. At a fixed PO2, such as around 60 mmHg, curve B has a lower percent saturation than curve A. Reasoning: Lower hemoglobin saturation means less oxygen is bound to hemoglobin at the same PO2. High CO2 lowers blood pH, corresponding to the right-shifted B curve, which reduces hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen. Therefore, under high-CO2 conditions, hemoglobin unloads/releases oxygen more readily.
